For centuries, the architecture of the firm has barely changed: hierarchies of people organized into departments and coordinated through bureaucracy.

AI agents are about to upend that.

We’re moving toward the self-driving company where humans exercise judgment and agents execute most of the work.

At Replit, we’re building the foundation for this new kind of company. We’re calling it “the Agent Habitat.”

Marc Andreessen wrote a fantastic piece placing this shift in the history of computing. Every major computing revolution began with chaos before businesses figured out how to harness it.

AI 代理即将颠覆这一点。

我们正迈向“自动驾驶公司”，其中人类行使判断力，而代理执行大部分工作。

x.text:
I built 𝚌𝚙𝚞-𝚌𝚑𝚊𝚝, a reproduction of @openai's findings of covert communication using the CPU.

It runs on a generic host with 2+ Firecracker microVMs with no internet access. Works on x86 and even my M5 chip.

I was able to chat via 3 separate mechanisms:
① CPU contention
② Cache eviction timing
③ DRAM bandwidth contention 

… across multiple CPUs, defeating all Firecracker's production recommendations (no SMT, no KSM, tenants pinned to different cores.)

Essentially, if shared hardware is involved, there's a good chance your agents can communicate covertly. And with really decent latency.

The good news: this is decidedly different from a *side-channel attack* where the agents could steal information (Meltdown/Spectre), a category of attack that providers like Vercel Sandbox mitigate. Further, in our real-world environment, these 'whispering' techniques are much harder to pull off and easier for us to monitor and detect (sampling hardware counters + lots of at-scale statistical data.)

Noteworthy: ironically, OpenAI and Anthropic's models refused to do this work. Open weight models got the job done. I'm worried the labs' stance might backfire and get in the way of helping developers build correct and secure systems. e.g: building a secure sandbox requires having this kind of analysis, and without it, we'll have a less secure world.

x.textZh:
我构建了 𝚌𝚙𝚞-𝚌𝚑𝚊𝚝，这是对 @openai 关于利用 CPU 进行隐蔽通信的研究成果的复现。

它在拥有 2 个以上 Firecracker 微虚拟机且无互联网访问的通用主机上运行。在 x86 架构甚至我的 M5 芯片上均可工作。

我通过 3 种不同的机制实现了聊天：
① CPU 争用
② 缓存驱逐计时
③ DRAM 带宽争用

……跨多个 CPU 运行，击败了 Firecracker 的所有生产环境建议（禁用 SMT、禁用 KSM、租户固定在不同核心上）。

本质上，如果涉及共享硬件，你的智能体很有可能进行隐蔽通信。而且延迟相当低。

好消息是：这显然不同于*侧信道攻击*，在侧信道攻击中，智能体可以窃取信息（如 Meltdown/Spectre），Vercel Sandbox 等提供商已经缓解了这类攻击。此外，在我们的真实世界环境中，这些“低语”技术的实施难度要大得多，而我们对其进行监控和检测则更容易（采样硬件计数器 + 大规模统计数据）。

值得注意的是：讽刺的是，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的模型拒绝执行这项工作。开源权重的模型完成了任务。我担心实验室的立场可能会适得其反，阻碍开发者构建正确且安全的系统。例如：构建安全沙箱需要这种分析，而如果没有它，我们将拥有一个安全性较低的世界。

x.text:
This is the key stat. The average Fortune 500 customer of Anthropic spends less than .1% of their expenses on Anthropic. 

While that number likely will eventually asymptote somewhere (token prices coming down, and other large enterprise spend areas not going away), there’s no reason it can’t be 10-50X higher than this, reaching a “mere” 1-5% of spend. Which would still be a fraction of what most startups are spending.

Thus, you can see how big of a divide there is between the frontier users of AI and the rest of the world still.

Today, only a microscopically small set of companies are actually using agents for large amounts of background tasks and inside of workflows that aren’t human prompted. This Fortune 500 spend is likely dominated by coding tasks and broad employee productivity use-cases.

But the big jump will come as these enterprises start to rewire their underlying processes for agents, which we’re now in the earliest stages of seeing. Agents processing large amounts of data in the enterprises; swarms doing coding, bio research, cyber, and other large fan out tasks; background workflows executing tasks in processes, and so on. All of these use cases generally are 100X bigger consumers of tokens, and much closer to direct ROI on the spend.

This S-1 gives you a sense of both the strength of the frontier lab business model - even amidst massive competition - and how early we are in the build out of AI.

x.textZh:
这才是关键数据。Anthropic 的 Fortune 500 客户平均在 Anthropic 上的支出不到其总支出的 0.1%。

虽然这个数字最终可能会在某处趋于稳定（代币价格下降，其他大型企业支出领域不会消失），但完全有理由相信它比当前水平高出 10-50 倍，达到“仅仅”1-5% 的支出比例。这仍然只是大多数初创公司支出的一小部分。

因此，你可以看出 AI 前沿用户与世界其余部分之间仍然存在巨大的鸿沟。

今天，只有极少量公司实际上在利用智能体处理大量后台任务以及非人工提示的工作流程。这些 Fortune 500 企业的支出可能主要由编码任务和广泛的员工生产力用例主导。

但巨大的飞跃将来自这些企业开始为智能体重构其底层流程，而我们目前正处于这一过程的最早阶段。智能体在企业中处理大量数据；群体进行编码、生物研究、网络安全和其他大规模发散任务；后台工作流在流程中执行任务，等等。所有这些用例通常消耗的代币量是当前的 100 倍，并且与支出的直接投资回报率更为接近。

这份 S-1 文件让你既看到了前沿实验室商业模式的力量——即便在激烈竞争之下——也让我们意识到，在 AI 的建设初期，我们才刚刚起步。

x.text:
The main thing I wanted to dig into @AnthropicAI's S-1 was the compute contracts..

A few things that stood out (built in conjuction with Opus 5.5):

> At June 30, Anthropic had $265.6B of purchase commitments and $321.4B of leases that hadn’t started. That’s a $587B subtotal, payable over years, including some conditional leases. The latest aggregate total is still blank in the filing.

> The contracts are very different. Google and Amazon require minimum spending regardless of usage. SpaceXAI’s agreements have a potential value of $120.5B, but either party can cancel on 90 days’ notice after initial locked periods end in January and March 2027.

> Anthropic Direct separates chips, buildings, power and operations into different contracts. It lets Anthropic reserve a building early and commit to chips later. It also means one supplier can start billing before the others are ready. Equipment rent can begin before the compute is usable.

> Broadcom’s $42B facility never hands Anthropic cash. Notes settle specific equipment rent bills. The facility excludes each equipment pod’s first quarterly payment and any rent due before it is ready for service. Anthropic has to find a way to fund those payments elsewhere.

> Those notes carry 9% interest, added to the balance quarterly, and can convert at 90% of the trailing 30-day average share price after IPO. New notes issued during specified revenue-breach periods get 13% interest and an 85% conversion price. The share-price measure is volume-weighted.

> That interest sits on top of the equipment lease’s own financing charge, whose rate is confidential. The investor chooses whether to convert the notes. Otherwise, principal and accumulated interest come due in cash.

> Anthropic treats Trainium, TPUs, NVIDIA and AMD GPUs as a shared fleet across model development, paying customers and internal use. It doesn’t disclose a fixed physical split between training and inference. The supplier bill can be fixed while the work assigned to the hardware changes.

> Revenue per dollar of total compute and infrastructure expense rose from $0.57 in Q2 2025 to $2.08 in Q2 2026. Pricing, utilization, technical improvements and when capacity arrives all affect that ratio. It’s a substantial improvement in monetizing the compute base.

> About 80% of H1 revenue was consumption-based. Most compute commitments however run for years. With quarterly releases, this bifurcation between usage and subscription will be interesting to monitor. 

Source: https://t.co/97KqkyyfpS

x.textZh:
我最想深入挖掘的是 @AnthropicAI 的 S-1 文件中的计算合同……

有几件事很突出（与 Opus 5.5 共同制定）：

> 截至 6 月 30 日，Anthropic 有 2656 亿美元的采购承诺和 3214 亿美元尚未开始的租赁。这是一个 5870 亿美元的子总额，需在多年内支付，包括一些有条件租赁。最新总计数在文件中仍为空白。

> 合同非常不同。Google 和 Amazon 要求无论使用情况如何都要最低支出。SpaceXAI 的协议潜在价值为 1205 亿美元，但任何一方都可以在 2027 年 1 月和 3 月初锁定期结束后以 90 天通知取消。

> Anthropic Direct 将芯片、建筑、电力和运营分开到不同的合同中。它让 Anthropic 提前预订建筑并稍后承诺芯片。这也意味着一个供应商可以在其他供应商准备好之前开始计费。设备租金可以在计算可用之前开始。

> Broadcom 的 420 亿美元设施从不向 Anthropic 提供现金。票据结算特定的设备租金账单。该设施排除每个设备舱的第一季度付款以及任何在设备准备好服务之前的租金。Anthropic 必须找到其他方式资助这些付款。

> 这些票据带有 9% 的利息，每季度添加到余额中，并可以在 IPO 后以过去 30 天平均股价的 90% 转换。在指定收入违约期间发行的新票据获得 13% 的利息和 85% 的转换价格。股价衡量标准是成交量加权。

> 这些利息位于设备租赁本身的融资费用之上，其利率保密。投资者可以选择是否转换票据。否则，本金和累计利息以现金到期。

> Anthropic 将 Trainium、TPU、NVIDIA 和 AMD GPU 视为模型开发、付费客户和内部使用的共享舰队。它不披露训练和推理之间的固定物理分割。供应商账单可以是固定的，而分配给硬件的工作会发生变化。

> 每美元总计算和基础设施支出的收入从 2025 年第二季度的 0.57 美元上升到 2026 年第二季度的 2.08 美元。定价、利用率、技术改进和容量到达时间都会影响该比率。这是对计算基础货币化的重大改进。

> 上半年约 80% 的收入基于使用量。然而，大多数计算承诺持续多年。随着季度发布，这种使用和订阅之间的 bifurcation 将是一个有趣的监控点。

We’re expanding Claude for Nonprofits with a plugin built with around 30 of them, adding skills for fundraising, marketing, and hiring grounded in each team’s context and AI policy: https://t.co/LWHcr1CT20 https://t.co/WHG2zRDyxO
x.bio: Claude is an AI assistant built by @anthropicai to be safe, accurate, and secure. Talk to Claude on https://t.co/ZhTwG8d1e5 or download the app.
